## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Esoteric *dhāraṇī* scripture translated by **Xuánzàng** ([玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98), 600/602–664), the great Tang Buddhist pilgrim and translator. Its preservation in the Esoteric volume 19 of the Taishō reflects the proto-tantric *dhāraṇī*-class character of the text — Xuánzàng's principal translation work was Yogācāra and *Prajñāpāramitā* doctrinal scriptures, but he also translated several *dhāraṇī* scriptures.

**Abstract**

The *Zhū fó xīn tuóluóní jīng* presents a *dhāraṇī*-recitation practice oriented to the Buddhas of the ten directions, accessing their cosmic compassion through the *xīn* ("heart" / *hṛdaya*) *dhāraṇī*. The text is one of the earliest Tang Chinese translations of a Buddhist *dhāraṇī* scripture in this style, predating the systematic Esoteric translations of the 8th century by some 70–100 years.

The translation dates from Xuánzàng's documented translation period at Chángān (645–664).
